In addition, geographic layers are prepared for woreda-, zone-, and region-level mapping, and application-wide settings such as date ordering and visual themes are initialized.

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
4.2 Dashboard structure and navigation
The dashboard was developed as a web-based interactive application using R Shiny. The application is organized into two main pages designed to support both user orientation and data exploration.
Overview page
The Overview page serves as the entry point to the dashboard and provides background information to help users understand the purpose, scope, and interpretation of the dashboard outputs.
The page includes the following sections:

About the dashboard
Data sources
Key indicators
Methodological notes and
Dashboard user guide

This page is intended to provide contextual information and support consistent interpretation of dashboard outputs.
Dashboard page
The Dashboard page contains all interactive visualizations and analytical outputs. It is organized into a sidebar panel containing user-defined filters and a main panel displaying a map, key performance indicators (KPIs), and charts.
Sidebar filters
The sidebar contains three groups of filters:
Geographic filters

Region
Zone
Woreda

These filters allow users to view data at different administrative levels and geographic locations.
Time filters

Gregorian year
Ethiopian Fiscal Year (EFY)
Month

These filters enable temporal analysis of malaria indicators.
Reporting filters

Facility type

The facility type filter is used only for reporting completeness and timeliness indicators. All other filters apply across all dashboard components.
Dashboard outputs
The main dashboard panel is organized into four rows of analytical outputs.
Row 1

Geographic map
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Row 2

Malaria testing and Test Positivity Rate (TPR)
Species proportion

The testing and TPR visualization combines malaria testing volume as a bar chart with TPR displayed as a line on a secondary axis.
Row 3

Parasite incidence per 1,000 population
Malaria mortality rate per 100,000 population at risk

Row 4

Reporting completeness
Reporting timeliness

Visualization modes
All dashboard charts include a display toggle that allows users to switch between:

Aggregate view and
Monthly trend view

The aggregate view summarizes indicator values over the selected period and geography, while the monthly view displays temporal trends across individual months.

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.1 Malaria Cases
Confirmed Malaria Cases
Confirmed malaria cases include all laboratory-confirmed malaria infections reported through HMIS, regardless of species.
Clinical Malaria Cases
Clinical malaria cases refer to malaria diagnoses made without parasitological confirmation.
All Malaria Cases
All malaria cases represent the total malaria burden reported through HMIS and are calculated as:
All Cases = Confirmed Cases + Clinical Cases

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.2 Malaria Deaths
Malaria deaths are defined as inpatient malaria-related deaths reported through the HMIS disease surveillance system.

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.3 Test Positivity Rate (TPR)
The Test Positivity Rate (TPR) measures the proportion of malaria tests that yield a positive result.
TPR = Positive Malaria Tests/Total malaria test performed x 100
Where:
- Positive malaria tests = laboratory-confirmed positive malaria tests
- Total malaria tests performed = all malaria diagnostic tests (microscopy and/or RDT)

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.4 Species Distribution
Species proportions describe the relative contribution of each malaria species among confirmed malaria cases.
Plasmodium falciparum Proportion = Pf cases/Total confirmed cases*100
Plasmodium vivax Proportion = Pv cases/Total confirmed cases*100
Mixed malaria (pf/pv) Proportion = Mixed cases/Total confirmed cases*100
Total Confirmed Cases = Pf + Pv + Mixed + P. malariae + P. ovale

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.5 Annual Parasite Incidence (API)
The dashboard uses adjusted malaria cases to account for clinically diagnosed malaria cases.
Adjusted malaria cases are calculated as:
Adjusted Cases = Confirmed Cases + (TPR × Clinical Cases)
Annual Parasite Incidence (API) is then calculated as:
API = Adjusted Cases/ Total Population × 1000 and expressed as cases per 1,000 population.

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.6 Annualized Monthly Parasite Incidence
For monthly dashboard displays, incidence is annualized to facilitate comparison with annual incidence targets.
Annualized monthly incidence = (Adjusted cases X n/12)/Total population X 1000
Where:
n = annualization factor used to project the observed reporting period to a 12-month equivalent

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.7 Malaria Mortality Rate
The malaria mortality rate is calculated using the population at risk as the denominator.
In accordance with the National Malaria Strategic Plan,the population at risk is defined as:  Population at Risk = Total Population × 69%
The mortality rate is calculated as:
Motality_rate = In-patient malaria deaths/population at risk X 100,000 and expressed as deaths per 100,000 population at risk.

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.8 Annualized Monthly Mortality Rate
For monthly dashboard displays, mortality is annualized using the same approach applied to incidence.
Annualized monthly mortality = (inpatient malaria deaths X n/12)/population at risk X 100,000
Where:
n = annualization factor used to project the observed reporting period to a 12-month equivalent

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.9 Reporting Completeness
Reporting completeness measures the proportion of expected reports that were submitted.
Reporting completeness = Actual reports/Expected reports X 100

title: National Malaria Elimination Program Dashboard: Technical Documentation and User Guide
text:
5.10 Reporting Timeliness
Reporting timeliness measures the proportion of expected reports that were submitted on time.
Reporting timeliness = Reports received on time/Expected reports X 100
Notes on Reporting Indicators
Reporting completeness and reporting timeliness are assessed using only the HMIS service reporting dataset. Both the numerator and denominator values are system-generated by DHIS2 and are not calculated manually within the dashboard.
These indicators assess reporting performance rather than malaria burden and are displayed separately from surveillance and service delivery indicators.

title: NMEP Monthly Bulletin Workflow
text:
This document serves as a workflow, sustainability, and handover guide for the production of the National Malaria Elimination Program (NMEP) Monthly Bulletin. Its purpose is to ensure continuity of bulletin production and enable future analysts to independently generate subsequent editions using a standardized and reproducible process.
The examples presented throughout this guide are based on the April 2026 bulletin production cycle and are provided solely for illustrative purposes. For future bulletin cycles, all month-specific references, file names, folder names, filtering criteria, plot labels, figure titles, and output file names should be updated to reflect the reporting month under analysis.
For example:

April 2026 bulletin: Apr-2026 compared with Apr-2025
May 2026 bulletin: May-2026 compared with May-2025
June 2026 bulletin: Jun-2026 compared with Jun-2025

Prior to running the workflow each month, users should verify that:

The most recent HMIS dataset has been downloaded, and cleaned.
The reporting month and corresponding comparison month from the previous year have been correctly specified.
Output folders and file naming conventions correspond to the reporting period.
Figure titles, labels, and captions accurately reflect the reporting month.
KPI calculations and visualizations are generated using the correct month-year combination.

Following these steps will help ensure consistency, accuracy, and comparability across bulletin editions over time.

Review of all figures, including titles, labels, and annotations for accuracy and clarity

These checks ensure the reliability of the bulletin and maintain consistency across monthly reporting cycles.

1.Malaria trend before and after non-HRP RDT roll out in Ethiopia
This research is an observational study which assessed the status of key HMIS malaria indicators pre and post non-HRP RDT rollout in Ethiopia.

Effect of the targeted cluster initiative on malaria indicators in Ethiopia
This research employed a non-randomized controlled before-and-after (CBA) study design to assess changes in malaria outcomes during and after the Targeted Cluster Initiative (TCI), a six-month intervention launched in June 2024 in Ethiopia in response to the country’s malaria resurgence. The study aimed to generate an accessible evidence base to inform the planning and implementation of future malaria response interventions.
